mainTopic: Aggadot about שמשון, five people struck through their special feature, תמנה and תמר, and the אשל of אברהם
overview: This amud is full of stories and lessons about שמשון and others. First the גמרא finishes explaining that אבימלך's oath to אברהם no longer protected the פלשתים, and that is why שמשון punished them with foxes, an animal that 'turns back'. It also tells of the blessing ה׳ gave the young שמשון, his last prayer, the huge width of his shoulders, and what 'grinding in prison' really means. רבי יוחנן adds that שמשון judged like ה׳, that his name reflects ה׳ as a 'sun and shield', and that he limped on both legs. A ברייתא then lists five people who were struck through the very feature they were known for, and the גמרא proves each one, ending with אסא's gout and his sin of drafting תלמידי חכמים. Next, the גמרא gives three answers to why one פסוק says people went 'down' to תמנה and another says 'up'. It brings three readings of 'פתח עינים' in the story of תמר and יהודה. Finally it explains the אשל אברהם planted as an orchard or an inn. ריש לקיש's new reading of 'ויקרא' begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The oath of אבימלך was undone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a teaching from the previous lines: the oath אבימלך made with אברהם was undone, and it quotes the oath itself as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The oath of אבימלך was undone, as it is written: 'That you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my grandson.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a thought from the previous lines. It says the old oath between אבימלך and אברהם was no longer binding by the time of שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימלך asked אברהם to swear not to harm him or his descendants. The פסוק only names a son and a grandson, so the oath had limits. Because the פלשתים themselves broke the peace by oppressing ישראל, the oath no longer protected them, and שמשון was free to fight them.

keyTerms.meaning: the פלשתי king who made a treaty with אברהם

steps.whyThisMatters: This broken oath comes back at the end of this section. It explains why שמשון chose foxes.

phrases.english: The oath of Avimelech was undone,
as it is written:
"That you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my son, nor with my grandson."
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:23. Literally it says 'if you deal falsely,' which is the way an oath is worded.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּחַל שְׁבוּעָתוֹ שֶׁל אֲבִימֶלֶךְ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the פסוק about שמשון from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oath between אבימלך and אברהם no longer bound ישראל in שמשון's time.

steps.title: What blessing did ה׳ give the young שמשון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that ה׳ blessed the growing שמשון and asks what that blessing was.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the child grew, and ה׳ blessed him.' With what did He bless him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק and asks a question about it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ blessed שמשון but does not say how. The גמרא wants to know what specific blessing is meant.

phrases.english: "And the child grew, and the Lord blessed him."
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:24

phrases.english: With what did He bless him?

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה בֵּרְכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new פסוק in שמשון's story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly was the blessing ה׳ gave שמשון as he grew?

steps.title: He was blessed with physical strength and fertility
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב answers that ה׳ blessed שמשון in his body: his body was like a grown man's and his seed was plentiful.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: He blessed him in his body. His organ was like that of grown men, and his seed was like a flowing river.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The blessing was physical: even though שמשון was young, his body was like a grown man's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the blessing to 'the child grew.' רב reads it as a blessing of early physical maturity and strong fertility. This fits the theme of שמשון's unusual physical strength.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
That He blessed him in his organ:
His organ was like that of grown men,
phrases.notes: Literally 'like people,' meaning like adults, even though he was still young.

phrases.english: and his seed was like a flowing river.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, שֶׁבֵּרְכוֹ בְּאַמָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing was physical: early adult maturity and abundant fertility.

steps.title: שמשון's last prayer: remember my selfless service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes שמשון's final prayer, and רב explains that 'remember me' meant: remember the years I judged ישראל without asking anyone for even a small favor.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And שמשון called to ה׳ and said: ה׳ אלהים, please remember me and please strengthen me just this once, and let me take revenge on the פלשתים for one of my two eyes.' רב said: שמשון said before הקדוש ברוך הוא: Master of the world, remember for me the twenty-two years that I judged ישראל, and I never told even one of them, 'Move a stick for me from one place to another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes שמשון's prayer just before he died. רב explains what שמשון was asking ה׳ to 'remember.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Remember me' is vague, so רב fills it in. שמשון pointed to his merit: he led ישראל for many years and never used his position to ask for even the smallest favor. He used that merit to ask for strength one last time.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the merit of a leader who serves the people without taking anything for himself.

phrases.english: "And Samson called to the Lord
and said: Lord God,
please remember me and please strengthen me
only this one time,
and let me take one revenge
for my two eyes from the Philistines."
phrases.notes: שופטים 16:28

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר שִׁמְשׁוֹן לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Samson said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
remember for me the twenty-two years
phrases.notes: This is רב's explanation of 'זׇכְרֵנִי', what שמשון wanted remembered.

phrases.english: that I judged Israel,
and I did not say to even one of them,
'Move a stick for me from one place to another.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אָמַר שִׁמְשׁוֹן לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to another פסוק in שמשון's life, his final prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמשון asked ה׳ to remember his years of leading ישראל without ever asking for any favor.

steps.title: Why did שמשון use foxes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק that שמשון caught three hundred foxes and asks what was special about foxes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And שמשון went and caught three hundred foxes.' What is different about foxes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about שמשון using foxes to burn the פלשתים' fields and asks why he picked foxes. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Any animal could carry a torch, so the גמרא assumes the choice of foxes has a meaning. It asks what that meaning is.

phrases.english: "And Samson went
and caught three hundred foxes."
phrases.notes: שופטים 15:4

phrases.english: What is different about foxes?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא שׁוּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to an earlier episode in שמשון's story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did שמשון specifically choose foxes to punish the פלשתים?

steps.title: An animal that turns back punishes those who turned back on their oath
steps.stepSummary: רבי איבו בר נגדי in the name of רבי חייא בר אבא explains that שמשון chose an animal that turns back to punish the פלשתים, who went back on their oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי איבו בר נגדי said in the name of רבי חייא בר אבא: שמשון said, Let the one that turns backward come and take punishment from the פלשתים, who went back on their oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why foxes were chosen. The fox 'turns back,' and the פלשתים 'turned back' on their oath, so the punishment matched the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to step 1: the פלשתים broke the oath of אבימלך. שמשון chose a punishment that matched their behavior. An animal known for going backward punished a people who backed out of their promise.

keyTerms.meaning: and let him take punishment, collect payment
they went back on their oath

steps.whatToRemember: The broken oath of אבימלך runs through this section. It explains why the oath no longer protected the פלשתים and why שמשון punished them with foxes, measure for measure.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the idea of מדה כנגד מדה (measure for measure): the punishment mirrors the wrong that was done.

phrases.english: Rabbi Aivu bar Nagdi said
that Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said:
Samson said:
Let the one that turns backward come,
phrases.notes: He means the fox.

phrases.english: and take punishment from the Philistines
who went back on their oath.
phrases.notes: This is the oath of אבימלך from the start of this section.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַיְּבוּ בַּר נַגְדִּי אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: אָמַר שִׁמְשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and links back to the broken oath in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Foxes turn backward, matching the פלשתים who went back on their oath. The punishment fit the wrong.

steps.title: The width of שמשון's shoulders
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון החסיד says שמשון's shoulders were sixty אמות wide. He proves it from the city gates of עזה that שמשון carried on his shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון החסיד said that שמשון's shoulders were sixty אמות wide. The פסוק says he pulled out the doors of the city gate and put them on his shoulders. We have a tradition that the doors of עזה were at least sixty אמות wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes how huge שמשון's body was. It proves the size from a פסוק plus a known tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two parts. The פסוק says שמשון put the gate doors 'on his shoulders', so his shoulders must have been as wide as the doors. A tradition says the doors of עזה were at least sixty אמות, so his shoulders were sixty אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: A measurement, about the length of a forearm
And we have a tradition (something passed down, not learned from a פסוק)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon the Pious said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כְּתֵיפָיו שֶׁל שִׁמְשׁוֹן שִׁשִּׁים אַמָּה הָיָה,
phrases.english: The space between Shimshon's shoulders was sixty amos,
as it says: "And Shimshon lay until midnight,

phrases.aramaic: וַיָּקׇם בַּחֲצִי הַלַּיְלָה וַיֶּאֱחֹז בְּדַלְתוֹת שַׁעַר הָעִיר
phrases.english: and he got up at midnight and grabbed the doors of the city gate
and the two doorposts, and pulled them out together with the bar,
and put them on his shoulders"
phrases.notes: שופטים 16:3

phrases.aramaic: וּגְמִירִי דְּאֵין דַּלְתוֹת עַזָּה פְּחוּתוֹת מִשִּׁשִּׁים אַמָּה.
phrases.english: and we have a tradition that the doors of Azah were not less than sixty amos.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הֶחָסִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of teachings about שמשון, going back to the theme of his amazing body from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמשון's shoulders were sixty אמות wide, as shown by his carrying the sixty-אמה gates of עזה on them.

steps.title: What 'grinding in prison' really means
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that 'grinding' in the פסוק about שמשון in prison means forbidden relations: the פלשתים brought their wives to him so they would have children from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says שמשון was 'grinding in the prison'. רבי יוחנן said: 'grinding' is a word for sin, like the פסוק in איוב, 'Let my wife grind for another man.' This teaches that every פלשתי brought his wife to the prison so she would become pregnant from שמשון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about שמשון in prison, and רבי יוחנן explains a hidden meaning of the word 'grinding'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, 'grinding' sounds like simple hard labor at a mill. רבי יוחנן shows from a פסוק in איוב that the same word is used for forbidden relations. So the פסוק is really saying the פלשתים wanted children from the powerful שמשון.

keyTerms.meaning: A word that refers to sin, here forbidden relations

phrases.english: "And he was grinding in the prison."
phrases.notes: שופטים 16:21

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
"Grinding" is nothing but a word for sin,
and so the verse says: "Let my wife grind for another man."
phrases.notes: איוב 31:10

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד הֵבִיא לוֹ
phrases.english: This teaches that each and every one brought to him
his wife, to the prison,
so that she would become pregnant from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין טְחִינָה אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן עֲבֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new פסוק about שמשון, from the end of his life after he was captured.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Grinding' means forbidden relations: the פלשתים brought their wives to שמשון in prison to have children from him.

steps.title: רב פפא's folk saying: give a person more of what he likes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא connects רבי יוחנן's teaching to a popular saying: bring wine to the wine-drinker and figs to the digger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this is what people say: in front of a wine drinker, put wine; in front of a digger, put figs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds a folk saying that fits what רבי יוחנן just taught about שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמשון had always been drawn to פלשתי women. In prison, the פלשתים brought him even more of them. The saying means: people give a person more of what he already wants.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (a common folk saying)
One who digs or hoes the ground
Figs (a cake or cluster of figs)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is what people say:
In front of one who drinks wine — wine;
in front of a digger — (figs).
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. The idea is the same: people bring someone more of what he already craves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a folk saying that matches רבי יוחנן's explanation in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What happened to שמשון fits the saying that people give a person more of what he already likes.

steps.title: A man who is unfaithful will find his wife unfaithful
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that whoever is unfaithful will have a wife who is unfaithful to him. He proves it from two פסוקים in איוב next to each other, and adds a folk saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: anyone who is unfaithful, his wife will be unfaithful to him. The פסוק in איוב says, 'If my heart was tempted by a woman and I waited at my neighbor's door,' and right after it says, 'Let my wife grind for another man and let others kneel over her.' People say: he is among the pumpkins, and his wife is among the zucchinis.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן uses the same פסוק about 'grinding' to teach a general lesson about faithfulness in marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In איוב, the first פסוק describes the man's own sin, and the next פסוק describes his wife sinning with others. Putting them side by side shows that the punishment matches the sin. The folk saying makes the same point: the wife ends up doing what the husband does.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who is unfaithful — his wife is unfaithful to him,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the standard גמרא, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean the same thing.

phrases.english: as it says: "If my heart was tempted by a woman
and I lay in wait at my neighbor's door,"
and it is written: "Let my wife grind for another man
and let others kneel over her."
phrases.notes: These are איוב 31:9 and 31:10, right next to each other.

phrases.english: And this is what people say:

phrases.aramaic: אִיהוּ בֵּי קָארֵי, וְאִיתְּתֵיהּ בֵּי בוּצִינֵי.
phrases.english: He is among the pumpkins, and his wife is among the zucchinis.
phrases.notes: These are two similar vegetables. She ends up doing just what he does.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַמְזַנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק from step 8 ('Let my wife grind for another') to teach a separate, general lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever is unfaithful will be punished measure for measure: his wife will be unfaithful to him.

steps.title: שמשון judged ישראל like ה׳ does
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן praises שמשון: he judged ישראל like their Father in Heaven, learned from יעקב's blessing to שבט דן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: שמשון judged ישראל like their Father in Heaven, as it says: 'Dan will judge his people like the One.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to praising שמשון, with another teaching from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמשון came from שבט דן. The פסוק says דן will judge 'like the One', and רבי יוחנן reads 'the One' as ה׳, who is One. So שמשון judged with fairness like ה׳'s.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְשׁוֹן דָּן אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: Shimshon judged Israel like their Father in Heaven,
as it says: "Dan will judge his people like the One, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:16. 'The One' is read as ה׳, who is One.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שִׁמְשׁוֹן דָּן אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side lesson in step 10 to praising שמשון as a judge, like step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמשון, from שבט דן, judged ישראל with fairness like ה׳.

steps.title: שמשון is named after ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says שמשון was called by הקדוש ברוך הוא's name, since a פסוק calls ה׳ a 'sun' (שמש).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: שמשון was called by the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא, as it says: 'For ה׳ אלהים is a sun and a shield.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a bold claim about the name שמשון. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name שמשון sounds like 'שמש', sun. A פסוק in תהלים calls ה׳ a 'sun', so רבי יוחנן says שמשון carries ה׳'s name.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְשׁוֹן עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְרָא,
phrases.english: Shimshon is called by the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה׳ אֱלֹהִים וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: as it says: "For ה׳ Elokim is a sun and a shield, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 84:12. The word for sun, שמש, sounds like שמשון.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שִׁמְשׁוֹן עַל שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another praise of שמשון from רבי יוחנן, this time about his name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name שמשון comes from ה׳'s description as a 'sun'.

steps.title: Then his name should not be erasable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן: if שמשון is truly ה׳'s name, it would be forbidden to erase it, like ה׳'s holy names.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the name should not be allowed to be erased!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the claim in step 12 by showing a strange result that would follow from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳'s holy names may not be erased. If 'שמשון' were really ה׳'s name, the same rule would apply to it. But nobody treats שמשון's name that way, so the claim cannot be meant literally.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (if we accept what you just said)

phrases.english: But if so, it should not be erased!
phrases.notes: ה׳'s holy names may not be erased, so this would have to apply to שמשון's name too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, לֹא יִמָּחֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that שמשון is called by ה׳'s name.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were truly ה׳'s name, it would have the holiness of a Divine name and could not be erased. That is clearly not so.

steps.title: His name is only similar to ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the statement: שמשון's name is like ה׳'s name, because just as ה׳ protects the whole world, שמשון protected ישראל in his generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his name is similar to the name of הקדוש ברוך הוא. Just as הקדוש ברוך הוא protects the whole world, so שמשון protected ישראל in his generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing the claim: the name is not actually ה׳'s name, it only reflects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fix is the word 'similar'. שמשון's name is not a holy name, so it may be erased. But it hints at the פסוק 'a sun and a shield': like ה׳ shields the world, שמשון shielded ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: שמשון's name is not a holy name of ה׳. It only reflects ה׳'s quality of protecting: as ה׳ shields the world, שמשון shielded ישראל in his time.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: מֵעֵין שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Rather: it is similar to the name of the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: מָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵגֵין עַל כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
phrases.english: just as the Holy One, Blessed be He, protects the entire world,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שִׁמְשׁוֹן מֵגֵין בְּדוֹרוֹ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: so too Shimshon protected Israel in his generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מֵעֵין שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by changing the wording of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the statement: 'called by ה׳'s name' becomes 'similar to ה׳'s name'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמשון's name is actually a name of ה׳, so it would have to be holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The name only reflects ה׳'s quality of protection ('a sun and a shield'), so it is not holy and may be erased.

steps.title: בלעם limped on one leg and שמשון on both
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that בלעם was lame in one leg and שמשון was lame in both legs. He learns each one from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: בלעם limped on one leg, because the פסוק says 'he went limping' (שֶׁפִי). שמשון limped on both legs, because the פסוק calls him 'שְׁפִיפֹן', a doubled form of that word.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds another teaching, this time about a physical detail: בלעם and שמשון were both lame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שֶׁפִי by בלעם is read as 'limping', so he limped on one leg. The word שְׁפִיפֹן in יעקב's blessing to דן, which was about שמשון, repeats the sound 'שפ', so רבי יוחנן reads it as a double limp, meaning both legs.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of snake; read here as a 'double limp'
The non-Jewish prophet who tried to curse ישראל

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Bilam was lame in one of his legs,
as it says: "And he went limping."
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:3

phrases.english: Shimshon was lame in both of his legs,
as it says: "A horned snake on the path."
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:17. The word שפיפון sounds like שפי said twice, so he limped twice, on both legs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement of רבי יוחנן about שמשון, continuing his series of teachings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בלעם limped on one leg (שֶׁפִי) and שמשון limped on both legs (שְׁפִיפֹן, a doubled form).

steps.title: Five people struck through their special feature
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that five people were created with a feature that reflected heavenly glory, and each was later struck through that same feature: שמשון, שאול, אבשלום, צדקיה, and אסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Five people were made with something like a heavenly model, and all of them were struck through it. שמשון in his strength, שאול in his neck, אבשלום in his hair, צדקיה in his eyes, and אסא in his feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a list of five people. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא proves each case from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these five had a special gift that was like a reflection of ה׳'s glory. The ברייתא's point is that the very gift that made them stand out is what brought about their downfall.

keyTerms.meaning: A model or reflection of what is Above
דוד המלך's son, known for his long hair
The last king of יהודה before the destruction

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Five people were created
with something like a model of Above,
phrases.notes: Each one had a special gift that looked like a reflection of heavenly glory.

phrases.english: and all of them were struck through those very things.
Shimshon in his strength, Shaul in his neck,

phrases.aramaic: אַבְשָׁלוֹם בִּשְׂעָרוֹ, צִדְקִיָּה בְּעֵינָיו, אָסָא בְּרַגְלָיו.
phrases.english: Avshalom in his hair, Tzidkiyahu in his eyes, Asa in his feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching that still includes שמשון, now listed with four others
steps.whyThisMatters: This list frames the next several steps, which prove each of the five cases from a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five people had a heavenly-like feature and were struck through it: שמשון in strength, שאול in neck, אבשלום in hair, צדקיה in eyes, אסא in feet.

steps.title: Proof that שמשון was struck through his strength
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the first case on the list: שמשון lost his strength, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמשון was struck through his strength, as it is written: 'And his strength left him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the ברייתא's list one by one, beginning with שמשון, and shows a פסוק for each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמשון's special gift was his strength. The פסוק in שופטים tells how his strength left him, which led to his downfall, so the gift itself became the place where he was struck.

phrases.english: Shimshon in his strength,
as it is written: "And his strength left him."
phrases.notes: שופטים 16:19

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁמְשׁוֹן בְּכֹחוֹ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the first item in the ברייתא's list
steps.raayaObject: That שמשון was struck through his strength

steps.title: Proof that שאול was struck through his neck
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the second case: שאול was struck in his neck when he fell on his sword.
steps.simpleTranslation: שאול was struck through his neck, as it is written: 'And שאול took the sword and fell on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second name on the list, שאול, and brings a פסוק for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול was known for being taller than everyone from his shoulders up, so his neck was his special feature. The גמרא reads his falling on the sword as the sword striking him there, so the gift became the place of his downfall.

phrases.english: Shaul in his neck,
as it is written:
"And Shaul took the sword and fell on it."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 31:4. The גמרא understands that he fell on the sword with his neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאוּל בְּצַוָּארוֹ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues proving the ברייתא's list, moving from שמשון to שאול
steps.raayaObject: That שאול was struck through his neck
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 31:4, 'וַיִּקַּח שָׁאוּל אֶת הַחֶרֶב וַיִּפֹּל עָלֶיהָ'

steps.title: אבשלום was struck through his hair
steps.stepSummary: The third case on the list, אבשלום, was struck through his hair. The proof will come later in the גמרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבשלום was struck through his hair, as we will explain later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third name on the ברייתא's list, אבשלום. It does not give the proof here and says it will come later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person on the list had a special feature and was later struck through it. For אבשלום that feature was his hair. Instead of quoting a פסוק now, the גמרא postpones the proof because the topic comes up again later.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד's son, famous for his beautiful hair
as we will say later on

phrases.english: Avshalom, in his hair,
as we will say further on.
phrases.notes: The proof isn't given here. The גמרא will talk about אבשלום's hair later.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבְשָׁלוֹם בִּשְׂעָרוֹ, כִּדְבָעֵינַן לְמֵימַר קַמַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues down the ברייתא's list after שמשון and שאול.
steps.raayaObject: That אבשלום was struck through his hair
steps.raayaSupportSource: Postponed to a later discussion in the גמרא

steps.title: צדקיהו was struck through his eyes
steps.stepSummary: The fourth case, צדקיהו, was struck through his eyes. The proof is the פסוק saying his eyes were blinded.
steps.simpleTranslation: צדקיהו was struck through his eyes, as the פסוק says: 'And he blinded the eyes of צדקיהו.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the fourth case on the list. It shows from a פסוק that צדקיהו was struck in his eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said צדקיהו's special feature was his eyes. The פסוק shows that this same feature was where he was punished, because his eyes were put out.

keyTerms.meaning: The last king of יהודה before the חורבן

phrases.english: Tzidkiyahu, in his eyes,
as it is written: 'And he blinded the eyes of Tzidkiyahu.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 25:7

steps.triggerLanguage: צִדְקִיָּה בְּעֵינָיו, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next case on the same list.
steps.raayaObject: That צדקיהו was struck through his eyes

steps.title: אסא was struck through his feet with gout
steps.stepSummary: The fifth case, אסא, was struck in his feet, as the פסוק says. רב adds that the illness was פדגרא (gout).
steps.simpleTranslation: אסא was struck through his feet, as it says: 'Only in his old age he was sick in his feet.' And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: this means gout took hold of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the last case on the list, אסא, from a פסוק about his feet. Then רב names the specific illness he had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says אסא was 'sick in his feet.' רב tells us what the sickness was: פדגרא, a painful disease of the feet and joints. This sets up the next few questions about that illness.

keyTerms.meaning: Gout, a very painful foot and joint disease

phrases.english: Asa, in his feet,
as it is written: 'Only in the time of his old age
phrases.notes: מלכים א 15:23

phrases.english: he was sick in his feet.'
And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
That gout took hold of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָסָא בְּרַגְלָיו, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case on the ברייתא's list.
steps.raayaObject: That אסא was struck through his feet
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 15:23, explained by רב as פדגרא
steps.whatToRemember: All five people on the list were punished through the same feature they were known for: שמשון (strength), שאול (neck), אבשלום (hair), צדקיהו (eyes), אסא (feet).

steps.title: מר זוטרא asks what gout feels like
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא asks his father רב נחמן what פדגרא is like.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, son of רב נחמן, asked רב נחמן: What is gout like?
steps.whatsHappening: A son asks his father to describe the illness רב just mentioned. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple question for information, not a challenge. מר זוטרא wants to understand how painful אסא's punishment was.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, said to him,
to Rav Naḥman: What is gout like?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי פָּדַגְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about the illness named in the previous step.

steps.title: רב נחמן: like a needle in living flesh
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that gout feels like a needle stuck into living flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is like a needle in living flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers his son's question by describing the pain of gout.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture of a needle in living flesh shows that אסא's punishment was a sharp, constant pain, not a mild weakness.

phrases.english: He said to him: Like a needle in living flesh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּמַחַט בִּבְשַׂר הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Gout feels like a needle in living flesh

steps.title: How did רב נחמן know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב נחמן knew what gout feels like.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רב נחמן got his description from. This sets up three possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Describing someone else's pain needs a source. The גמרא wants to know whether this came from experience, from tradition, or from somewhere higher.

phrases.english: From where did he know?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא יָדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source of רב נחמן's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of רב נחמן's knowledge about gout

steps.title: Three explanations of how he knew
steps.stepSummary: There are three opinions: he had the illness himself, he heard it from his teacher, or ה׳ revealed it to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he suffered from it himself. Some say he heard it from his teacher. And some say: 'The secret of ה׳ is with those who fear Him, and He makes His covenant known to them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives three different answers to how רב נחמן knew what gout feels like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer is personal experience and the second is tradition from his רבי. The third uses a פסוק to say ה׳ shares hidden knowledge with those who fear Him, so רב נחמן knew through רוח הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: ה׳'s secret is with those who fear Him

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: מֵיחַשׁ הֲוָה חָשׁ בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: Some say: He himself suffered from it.
And some say: He heard it from his teacher.
And some say:
'The secret of ה׳ is with those who fear Him, and His covenant, to make it known to them.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 25:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: מֵיחַשׁ הֲוָה חָשׁ בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24's question with three options.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Personal experience, his teacher, or divine revelation

steps.title: אסא was punished for forcing תלמידי חכמים into labor
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that אסא was punished because he forced תלמידי חכמים to do the king's labor, as the פסוק shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: Why was אסא punished? Because he forced תלמידי חכמים to do labor, as it says: 'And King אסא proclaimed to all יהודה, no one was exempt.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the reason for אסא's punishment. He proves it from the פסוק describing אסא's call for workers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we knew how אסא was punished: in his feet. רבא adds why. He drafted everyone for forced labor, even תלמידי חכמים. רבא learns this from the words 'all יהודה' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rava taught:
For what reason was Asa punished?
Because he made Torah scholars do forced labor,
as it says: 'And King Asa proclaimed
phrases.notes: מלכים א 15:22

phrases.english: to all Judah, no one was exempt.'
phrases.notes: The word 'all' shows that even Torah scholars were taken. The next step asks what 'no one was exempt' adds.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרֵשׁ רָבָא: מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶעֱנַשׁ אָסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how אסא was punished to why he was punished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסא was punished for drafting תלמידי חכמים into forced labor
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how seriously חז"ל treat taking Torah scholars away from their learning.

steps.title: What does 'no one was exempt' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'אין נקי' add.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'no one was exempt' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the extra words 'אין נקי' come to include. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already said 'all יהודה.' The extra phrase 'no one was exempt' seems to add something more, and the גמרא wants to know what.

phrases.english: What is 'no one was exempt'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אֵין נָקִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the פסוק רבא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is included by the words אין נקי

steps.title: Even a groom and bride were taken
steps.stepSummary: רב says 'no one was exempt' means even a groom from his room and a bride from her חופה were drafted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Even a groom from his room and a bride from her חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains the extra words. אסא drafted even newlyweds, who normally would be exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls a new groom 'נקי,' meaning free from duties for his first year. 'אין נקי' means אסא ignored even that exemption. This shows how far his draft went.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Even a groom from his room
phrases.notes: The Torah calls a new groom נקי, free for his first year (דברים 24:5). That is the exemption אסא ignored.

phrases.english: and a bride from her wedding canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אֲפִילּוּ חָתָן מֵחֶדְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even newlyweds, who are normally exempt, were drafted

steps.title: Going down to תמנה or going up?
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק says שמשון went 'down' to תמנה, and another says יהודה went 'up' to תמנה. Which is it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And שמשון went down to תמנה.' And it is written: 'Behold, your father-in-law is going up to תמנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to שמשון and puts two פסוקים side by side. They seem to disagree about whether you go down or up to reach תמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A place cannot be both below and above the same road. The two פסוקים seem to contradict each other about where תמנה is. The question is implied and not spelled out, and the next step resolves it.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא never says 'there is a contradiction' out loud. The pattern 'כתיב... וכתיב' itself signals that two פסוקים are clashing.

phrases.english: It is written: 'And Samson went down to Timnah,'
phrases.notes: שופטים 14:1

phrases.english: and it is written: 'Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:13. The father-in-law here is יהודה, on his way to where he meets תמר.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב: ״וַיֵּרֶד שִׁמְשׁוֹן תִּמְנָתָה״, וּכְתִיב: ״הִנֵּה חָמִיךְ עֹלֶה תִמְנָתָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of שמשון after the side discussion about אסא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים about travel to תמנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק describes going down to תמנה and the other going up. They seem to contradict each other.

steps.title: Down for שמשון's disgrace, up for יהודה's rise
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that 'down' and 'up' describe each person's spiritual direction, not the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: שמשון, who was disgraced there, has 'going down' written about him. יהודה, who was raised up there, has 'going up' written about him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר settles the contradiction. The words are not about geography. They describe what happened to each person in תמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמשון fell spiritually in תמנה through the Philistine woman, so the פסוק says he went 'down.' יהודה rose in תמנה, so the פסוק says he went 'up.' Both פסוקים are true because they describe the people, not the land.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנ"ך's words 'down' and 'up' can describe a person's spiritual fall or rise, not just the direction of travel.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Samson, who was disgraced there,
going down is written about him.
Judah, who was elevated there,
going up is written about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שִׁמְשׁוֹן שֶׁנִּתְגַּנָּה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the words are spiritual, not geographic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'down' and 'up' describe the physical road to תמנה, so the פסוקים clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words describe שמשון's disgrace and יהודה's rise, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Two different towns named תמנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says there were two towns called תמנה. One was reached by going down, and one by going up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: There were two towns named תמנה. One you went down to, and one you went up to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the 'down' versus 'up' question from step 29. This answer is about the actual road, not about spiritual direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר explained the two words as spiritual. רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads them as plain geography: there were two different towns, so there is no contradiction. שמשון went to the one in a valley, and יהודה went to the one on a hill.

keyTerms.meaning: Timnah, the town both פסוקים mention

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
There were two Timnahs,
one reached by going down, and one reached by going up.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: שְׁתֵּי תִּמְנָאוֹת הָיוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer than רבי אלעזר to the same contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different places: the פסוקים are talking about two separate towns.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both פסוקים describe the trip to the same single town, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: There were two towns named תמנה, one low and one high.

steps.title: One תמנה on a hillside
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says there was only one תמנה, built on a slope. Coming from one side you go down to it, and coming from the other side you go up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: There was one תמנה. Someone coming from one side went down to it, and someone coming from the other side went up to it. Towns like this are ורדוניא, בי בארי, and the market of נרש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to the 'down' versus 'up' question. רב פפא keeps one town and explains the difference by which side you came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does not need two towns. One town on a hillside can be 'down' for one traveler and 'up' for another. He backs this up with towns his listeners knew that were built the same way.
steps.whatToRemember: Three answers to the 'down' versus 'up' question about תמנה: spiritual direction (רבי אלעזר), two towns (רבי שמואל בר נחמני), or one town on a slope (רב פפא).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
There was one Timnah,
one who came from this side went down,
phrases.notes: Literally it says 'this side' both times. He means one side, and then the other side.

phrases.english: and one who came from that side went up.

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן וַרְדּוֹנְיָא וּבֵי בָארֵי וְשׁוּקָא דְנַרֶשׁ.
phrases.english: For example: Vardonia, Bei Varei, and the market of Neresh.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: חֲדָא תִּמְנָה הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 31's two towns and says there was one town on a slope.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same place, different direction of approach.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Answering the contradiction needs two separate towns.
steps.terutzMaskana: One town on a hillside is 'down' from one side and 'up' from the other.

steps.title: תמר sat at the entrance of אברהם's tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'ותשב בפתח עינים.' רבי אלכסנדרי explains that תמר sat at the entrance of אברהם אבינו's home, a place every eye longs to see.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And she sat at the entrance of עינים.' רבי אלכסנדרי said: This teaches that she went and sat at the entrance of אברהם אבינו, a place that all eyes look forward to seeing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the תמר story and starts asking what 'פתח עינים' means. רבי אלכסנדרי gives the first explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עינים' means 'eyes.' רבי אלכסנדרי reads 'the entrance of eyes' as a place everyone wants to see, which is the doorway of אברהם. So תמר chose a holy, well-known spot to sit.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the entrance of eyes,' the place where תמר sat

phrases.english: "And she sat at the entrance of Einayim."
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:14, about תמר waiting for יהודה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri said:
This teaches that she went and sat herself down
at the entrance of Avraham our father,
a place that all eyes look forward to seeing.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַתֵּשֶׁב בְּפֶתַח עֵינַיִם״. אָמַר רַבִּי אֲלֶכְּסַנְדְּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where תמנה was to the next פסוק in the תמר story (בראשית 38:14).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'פתח עינים' is the entrance of אברהם אבינו, a place all eyes long to see.

steps.title: עינים is simply the name of a place
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין quotes רב: עינים is the real name of a town. He proves it from the list of towns in ספר יהושע, which includes 'העינם.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said in the name of רב: It is a place called עינים. And similarly the פסוק says: 'תפוח והעינם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of 'פתח עינים.' רב reads it simply, as the name of a town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלכסנדרי read 'eyes' as a hint. רב says there is no hint: עינים is a place name. His proof is a פסוק that lists a town called 'העינם' in the land of יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly the פסוק says (a supporting source)
Two town names from a list in ספר יהושע

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said in the name of Rav:
It is a place whose name is Einayim,
and similarly the פסוק says: "Tapuach and Ha'einam."
phrases.notes: יהושע 15:34

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חָנִין אָמַר רַב: מָקוֹם הוּא שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ עֵינַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a plainer reading of the same words that רבי אלכסנדרי explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עינים is a real town's name, as shown by 'העינם' in ספר יהושע.

steps.title: תמר's answers cleared every worry
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says 'עינים' means she gave 'eyes' to her words. Each time יהודה raised a reason she might be forbidden, she answered it: a convert, unmarried, an orphan, and pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: She gave 'eyes' to her words. When he asked to be with her, he said: Maybe you are not Jewish? She said: I am a convert. Maybe you are married? She said: I am not married. Maybe your father accepted קידושין for you? She said: I am an orphan. Maybe you are impure? She said: I am pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third explanation of 'פתח עינים.' רבי שמואל בר נחמני reads it as 'she opened up her words,' and then shows the conversation that proves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'פתח' means an opening and 'עינים' means her words were clear. יהודה checked four possible problems, and her four answers removed each one. This also shows that יהודה was careful not to do something forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked to be with her
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whatToRemember: Three readings of 'פתח עינים': the entrance of אברהם (רבי אלכסנדרי), a town called עינים (רב), or 'she gave eyes to her words' by answering all of יהודה's questions (רבי שמואל בר נחמני).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
She gave 'eyes' to her words.
phrases.notes: He reads 'פתח עינים' as her words opening the way, and the questions that follow show how.

phrases.english: When he asked to be with her, he said to her:
Maybe you are not Jewish?
She said to him: I am a convert.
Maybe you are a married woman?
She said to him: I am unmarried.
Maybe your father accepted betrothal for you?
She said to him: I am an orphan.
Maybe you are impure?
She said to him: I am pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: שֶׁנָּתְנָה עֵינַיִם לִדְבָרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of 'פתח עינים,' about her words rather than a place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'פתח עינים' means תמר's words opened the way by answering each of יהודה's concerns.

steps.title: אברהם planted an orchard in באר שבע
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the אשל אברהם planted was a full orchard with every kind of sweet fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'And he planted an אשל in באר שבע.' ריש לקיש says this teaches that אברהם made an orchard and planted every kind of sweet fruit in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new פסוק about אברהם, and ריש לקיש explains what the אשל was: a large orchard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A simple reading of 'אשל' could mean a single tree. ריש לקיש reads it as a whole orchard filled with many fruits, which fits the theme of אברהם's generous home from the earlier steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The thing אברהם planted in באר שבע; its exact meaning is discussed here
It teaches; the פסוק is showing us something

phrases.english: "And he planted an eshel in Be'er Sheva"
phrases.notes: בראשית 21:33.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
This teaches that he made an orchard,
and planted in it all kinds of sweet fruits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּטַּע אֶשֶׁל בִּבְאֵר שָׁבַע אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of תמר to a new פסוק about אברהם, continuing the theme of אברהם's home mentioned in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אשל was an orchard planted with all kinds of sweet fruits.

steps.title: Orchard or inn: a dispute about the word אשל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה disagree: one says אשל means an orchard, the other says it means an inn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה argue. One says the אשל was an orchard, and one says it was an inn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between two תנאים about what the word אשל means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion matches ריש לקיש: an orchard. The second opinion says אברהם built an inn, a place for guests to stay. We are not told which תנא holds which view.

keyTerms.meaning: An inn, a place where travelers stay
One said (used when we don't know which רבי said which opinion)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Nechemya disagree:
one said: an orchard,
phrases.notes: They are arguing about what the word אשל means.

phrases.english: and one said: an inn.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dispute of תנאים about the same word ריש לקיש explained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One view: אשל is an orchard. Other view: אשל is an inn.

steps.title: How can you 'plant' an inn?
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ויטע' fits an orchard well, but it seems strange for an inn.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says orchard, because the פסוק says 'he planted.' But for the one who says inn, what does 'he planted' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'inn' opinion using the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You plant trees, not buildings. So the word 'ויטע' seems to support the orchard view and to be hard for the inn view.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (sets up the side that has no problem)
According to the one who says

phrases.english: It works well for the one who said orchard,
that is why it is written "and he planted."
But for the one who said inn,
what is "and he planted"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פַּרְדֵּס הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב וַיִּטַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second opinion in step 37.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that אשל means an inn.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'ויטע' means planting, which fits trees, not a building.

steps.title: 'Planting' can mean setting up tents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows from דניאל that 'ויטע' is also used for pitching tents, so it can describe building an inn.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And he shall plant the tents of his palace.' So 'planting' can also mean setting up a dwelling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a פסוק where 'ויטע' is used for tents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In דניאל, the same word describes setting up tents, not planting trees. So the inn opinion can read 'ויטע אשל' as 'he set up a lodging place.'
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions fit the word 'ויטע': an orchard is planted, and an inn can be 'planted' like tents are set up.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And he shall plant the tents of his palace, etc."
phrases.notes: דניאל 11:45. Here 'planting' means setting up tents.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִכְתִיב וַיִּטַּע אׇהֳלֵי אַפַּדְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from another פסוק that the word has a wider meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ויטע' can only mean planting trees, so it cannot describe an inn.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ויטע' is also used for setting up tents, so it can describe building an inn.

steps.title: ריש לקיש begins rereading 'and he called'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rest of the פסוק, and ריש לקיש starts to say the word 'ויקרא' should be read differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק continues: 'And he called there in the name of ה׳, the Everlasting God.' ריש לקיש said: Do not read it as 'and he called,'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the same פסוק and sets up ריש לקיש's new reading. His full point continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אל תיקרי' means ריש לקיש will suggest reading the word in a different way to teach a lesson. Here we only hear which word he is rereading; the new reading comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as (introduces a different reading of a word)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תיקרי' does not mean the written פסוק is wrong. It is a way of drawing an extra lesson from how the word could be read.

phrases.english: "And he called there in the name of ה׳, the Everlasting God."
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, בראשית 21:33.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Do not read "and he called,"
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, where he says what to read instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּקְרָא שָׁם בְּשֵׁם ה׳ אֵל עוֹלָם אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אַל תִּיקְרֵי וַיִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the next words of the פסוק from step 36 and opens a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש begins to teach that 'ויקרא' should be read differently (completed on the next amud).
